newsitem.title: QATAR: GCC, Europe meeting to explore gas partnerships.
newsitem.headline: GCC, Europe meeting to explore gas partnerships.

text.p: Gulf Arab states seeking a share of the burgeoning European natural gas market are due to begin talks with the European Union on Sunday to explore strategic partnerships for the development of costly gas projects, officials said on Friday.

The two-day conference, organised by the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council and the European Commission, is to examine Europe's growing gas demand, potential supplies in the next decade and the importance of Gulf Arab states as long-term players in the international gas market.

"(The conference) will contribute to the promotion and establishment of partnership between the EU and the GCC in the gas sector," said Sheikh Abdullah bin Ahmed al-Thani, chairman of the conference steering committee.
The GCC states -- Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates -- already supply around 50 percent of Europe's oil.

"This will be achieved by...investigating prospects for gas network development in the GCC and the EU, as well as addressing the economic and financial aspects of developing new gas projects and transit routes," Sheikh Abdullah said.

A technical paper on the prospects of a GCC-EU gas pipe link is due to be presented at the conference. Also under discussion will be the current liquefied natural gas (LNG) situation, potential developments and the experiences of the GCC and the EU in financing their own gas projects.

GCC states control around 50 percent of the world's gas reserves and at least four of them -- Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE and Qatar -- are competing with each other and other producers from outside the region to market their gas worldwide.

Western Europe's gas consumption was expected to rise to around 500 billion cubic metres annually in 2010 from a current 330 billion cubic metres, and indigenous production was expected to remain stable at around 240 billion cubic metres a year, said Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah.
"This represents twice the expected level of imports in the Far East region and from this you can understand our great interest in the European market," he said.

In 1993, Qatar signed a letter of intent with Italy's Snam to set up a project, called Eurogas, to supply Europe with eight billion cubic metres of LNG. But the project failed to get off the ground because of a price dispute.
However, Qatari officials say there is a growing market for Gulf gas in Europe, and consumers will be ready to pay the international price once local supplies stagnate after 2005.

Qatar has sold its LNG to Japanese and South Koreans at $3.60 per million British Thermal Unit (BTU). In western Europe, a million BTU of piped gas costs an average of $2.5, an energy specialist said.
Pricing of gas will be a key issue at the Doha conference, said Abdulaziz al-Malki, also part of the steering committee.
Around 300 delegates -- 80 from the European Union -- are expected to attend the conference, entitled "EU-GCC: Extending the partnership to Natural Gas", al-Malki said.
